What is the logic for why docs#instSMulOfMul has priority less than 1000 (it's 910 in core)?

In Mathlib PR #34077 I made a copy of the instance with priority 1100 and it gives a 290G instruction speedup in mathlib; one file gets substantially slower but that's because that file has a declaration which is borked because of lean4#12102 ; the hack #34088 which works around this issue, in tandem with #34077, gives a saving in mathlib of 463.2G (see here ).

My argument for making the priority > 1000 in mathlib is "this instance is essentially always the right one when it applies, and is essentially always quick to fail when it isn't". Does this also apply to core and other applications? I am unclear about what the counterargument is, but presumably the instance is at 910 for a reason.

I write more about my thoughts here.
Looks like the instance was added in this commit with a priority of 910. Maybe @Kim Morrison remembers why?
Re-pinging @Kim Morrison
It's 910 in core only because I copy-pasted it from Mathlib. It's been that way since the port.
Let's see what the benchmarks on lean#13554 say.
Mathlib fails in Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Units.lean on lean-pr-testing-13554. Could someone interested investigate?

See https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/34077/changes

The core change fixes an instance diamond in mathlib.

The core change fixes an instance diamond in mathlib.

That's not true, it just breaks the test for that diamond
@Eric Wieser, if you understand what's going on here, could you tell me what to do next here?
A simple fix would be to replace the broken test with the full underlying term used on master
But also, we should do a benchmark with the core change and mathlib change applied simultaneously, and for the purpose of generating that we can temporarily disable the test.
Okay, my interpretation of that is that the next steps are at the Mathlib end, and I'm going to hope someone else does it. :-) Please ping me again if lean#13554 needs modifying or merging!

In fact, doesn't this mean that #38703 did something bad? I think that smul_eq_mul lemma is now different unintentionally.
There were two things there: a test of an instance diamond, and a useful proof of a lemma. The test of the instance diamond has been moved to a standalone example.
oh nevermind, I'm being dumb.
(In my head I thought that line 88 was removed because it had to be removed since the rfl now succeeded, but that's not the case)

It only has to be removed if lean#13554 gets merged, because then rfl will work; the diamond is still there (thanks Eric for putting me right there), it's just not exposed by the lemma any more (which could perhaps be removed if lean#13554 gets merged), but it is exposed by the example.
Jireh, your instinct is right, that lemma is now broken
#38732 has the actual fix

(possibly the fault of #38711 ?)

Jireh, your instinct is right, that lemma is now broken

You mean "now = post merging of lean#13554", right?
Right. If either lean#13554 or mathlib #38704 get merged then the lemma will still compile but its meaning will change (which we don't want to happen). I agree with Eric's fix.
And boy oh boy #38704 does look appealing...

It wouldn't surprise me if the core change does nothing if the mathlib PR (which makes the same change) is merged.
I've just rebased lean#13554 on nightly-with-mathlib, so hopefully it will get a builds-mathlib label soon.
